title: What Came Back Home
logline: A woman returns to her home village after years of work abroad, naming places before they come into view, and finds that some of what she remembers is no longer there to be seen.
human_question: When you remember a place, what exactly are you holding onto, if the place itself has already changed?

premise.story: A migrant worker returns home after years away. The journey home, the first sight of the house, and the gap between the village she describes from memory and the village that is actually there form the film.
premise.place: A rural home and the road leading to it, somewhere a family has waited years for a return.
premise.experience: The viewer travels between what someone remembers and what is actually in front of them, and feels how much of coming home is the mind meeting its own past.

concept_links.why: The source distinguishes sharply between remembering a place, an object that no longer exists, and meeting the place as it now stands, a present object, precisely the gap a long-absent return makes visible [C047-M:L9; C047-M:L11].

The source's account of mind-door processes, taking a past object, then its name, then its meaning, describes, in doctrinal terms, how recognition of a changed place is built up in stages rather than arriving all at once.

The source's account of the mind door taking objects across all three times, while the senses meet only the present, frames why a returnee can see a house from years ago even while standing in front of the house as it is now.

what_camera_could_observe: The journey from airport or bus stop toward the village
The returnee naming places before they come into view, and correcting herself when they don't match
The first sight of the house and family
What has changed and what has not, in the family's own account
Quiet moments of adjustment in the days that follow
what_must_be_real: The family's real situation and feelings; no staged reunion moment for the camera. The economic realities of migrant labour must not be glossed over for a sentimental arc.

possible_arc.opening: The journey home begins; memory runs ahead of the road.
possible_arc.turn: Something does not match what was remembered, a changed house, an absent neighbour, a grown child.
possible_arc.ending_open: The family's real adjustment, however it actually goes, closes the film.

position_hint: middle: an intimate family story built on memory and return, not an Object 5 acquisition moment.

requirements: A family with a member returning from long-term work abroad, willing to be filmed
Access to both the journey and the home over enough time to observe real adjustment
Careful, ongoing consent from the whole family, including any children

suggestions.name: A rural village in the North Western or North Central Province
suggestions.why: Regions with a long history of overseas labour migration and return.
suggestions.verify: A specific family and their willingness to be filmed over time are unconfirmed.

risks: Pathos-driven framing of migrant labour and family separation
Intruding on a family's private emotional adjustment
Implying the family's story is a lesson rather than their own life
drop_if: No family with a genuine, upcoming return is found
The family does not want their reunion and adjustment filmed
Access would require staging the return itself

connections.note: Both are about what the mind holds onto after contact has already ended, a place once seen, a sound once heard.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
